overview: The Maratha Empire challenged Mughal dominance and controlled much of the Indian subcontinent in the 18th century. Founded by Shivaji, it revived Hindu political power and developed innovative military and administrative systems.

items.text: Light cavalry tactics using speed, surprise and mountain terrain defeated heavier Mughal armies.
A network of hill forts across the Western Ghats provided strategic defense.
Shivaji crowned as Chhatrapati in a formal Hindu ceremony, asserting sovereign Hindu kingship.
The Ashtapradhan council of eight ministers created an efficient administrative system.
Marathi language and culture promoted as the basis of state identity.
Revenue system based on direct collection from peasants, bypassing feudal intermediaries.
The Maratha challenge fatally weakened the Mughal Empire.
Marathi regional identity and pride trace directly to this period.

fall.text: The Maratha Confederacy was defeated by the British East India Company in the Third Anglo-Maratha War.
